title: Qcqs rational finite-model inputs are locally generated by integral coefficient extensions
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $V$ [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$, the condensed ring of all continuous functions to the normed finite extension $E$, or let $\Lambda=\Omega^{\mathrm{fin}}$ be the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]: on a profinite set $S$ its sections are continuous functions $S\to\Omega$ whose image is contained in one finite subextension. This second coefficient ring is not the all-norm-continuous-function ring. Put $\mathcal F=\{E\}$ in the first case and let $\mathcal F$ be the set of all finite subextensions $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ of $\Omega$ in the second, in the universe [def-weil-size-convention]. For $F\in\mathcal F$ put $A=\mathcal O_F$ with its induced norm topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], pull these condensed rings back to $V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, and set $T_{F,V}(J)=\Lambda_V\otimes^L_{A_V}J$ in the ordinary unbounded module-object category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $\mathcal G_V$ consist of these objects for all $J\in\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(V,A)$, with the finite constant scalar-model constructibility and finite Tor amplitude of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Every object of $\mathcal G_V$ belongs to $\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(V,\Lambda)$, and every object of $\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(V,\Lambda)$ belongs to $\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal G_V)$. Here $\operatorname{Loc}$ is the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] of the ambient ordinary derived category containing $\mathcal G_V$ and closed under all small ambient coproducts; arbitrary $\Lambda_V$-linear morphisms are allowed. In the finite-extension case this agrees with [sk-def-localizing-closure]. The generation conclusion in fact uses only finitely many shifts and triangle extensions for each input. No descent of the input complex or its connecting morphisms to one finite coefficient field is asserted. No Noetherian, characteristic, dimension or invertibility-of-$\ell$ hypothesis on $V$ is imposed.

source.place: (2), coefficient devissage needed for the closed-complement generator calculation. Agent qcqs/all-continuous norm-topological generation lemma. Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach Theorem 7.7 supports the finite rational-field comparison; its Lemma 7.9 uses colimit topology and is NOT asserted to prove the norm-topological algebraic-closure clause here.

proof.text: For a generator represented by integral J, choose a Tor interval from J.property and apply qcqs_integral_scalar_extension_ctf for the specified coefficient inclusion. Transport bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude along its ambient isomorphism. For the closure coefficient identify coefficientMap of the composite with the composite pulled-back maps and use the derived scalar functor isomorphism.

Apply qcqs_constructible_integral_leaf_models to a constructible module M to get an actual finite qcqs open/closed tree with integral lisse leaf models. Apply qcqs_lattice_tree_reconstruction, supplying coefficient flatness at each path vertex from qcqs_integral_scalar_extension_ctf. Each branch model is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude and its derived scalar extension is the terminal branch object. It therefore lies in the specified generator predicate up to ambient isomorphism. Monotonicity of extensionProductIter transfers the finite reconstruction witness to the shift closure of the generators.

The property Q of being a finite extension product of shifted generators is isomorphism invariant. For a distinguished triangle, combine n and m extension products into n+1+m using extensionProductIter_add. Its zero case follows from the degree-zero zero constructible module and the isomorphism between zero objects. It is stable under shifts because every extensionProductIter of the shift closure is. Apply the existing bounded degreewise devissage theorem to the cohomology objects of K, using singleFunctors.shiftIso to put degree-zero sheaf constructions in degree q. This proves the finite-generation assertion without a Tor hypothesis on the input beyond the original statement.

For each localizing subcategory P containing the generators, shiftClosure_le_iff puts the shift closure in P, and extensionProductIter_le_of_isTriangulatedClosed2 puts every finite extension product in P. Quantify over P to obtain the localizing-closure assertion. This proves both unchanged coefficient cases; no maps descend to a common finite field.
